comment: A short SYNTHETIC act, not a real statute. Committing a real tax act risks a licensing problem and a large binary in the repo; a synthetic one is honest about what it is and can be written to match utils/taxActParse.ts's heading regex exactly, which is the thing being demonstrated. The parser is tuned for Indian/UK-style drafting ('Section 12(2)(a)') and does NOT match US IRC-style headings ('§ 61(a)(1)') - a documented limitation, not a bug - so the headings below use the form it parses. The seeder builds a minimal uncompressed PDF from this text and uploads it through the Document Vault, so the bytes are a real PDF with a real SHA-256.

body: Sample Business Taxation Act, 2019
An Act to consolidate the law relating to the taxation of business income, input credits and allowable deductions.
Section 1. Short title and commencement.
(1) This Act may be cited as the Sample Business Taxation Act, 2019.
(2) It shall come into force on the first day of April, 2019.
Section 2. Definitions.
(1) In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires -
(a) 'assessable business' means any trade, profession or vocation carried on with a view to profit;
(b) 'input credit' means tax borne on a qualifying supply received in the course of an assessable business;
(c) 'qualifying supply' means a supply of goods or services used wholly and exclusively for the purposes of an assessable business;
(d) 'prescribed period' means the period of twelve months ending on the thirty-first day of March.
Section 12. Allowable deductions.
(1) In computing the profits of an assessable business, there shall be allowed as a deduction any expenditure incurred wholly and exclusively for the purposes of that business.
(2) No deduction shall be allowed under sub-section (1) in respect of -
(a) expenditure of a capital nature, save as provided in Section 18;
(b) entertainment expenditure, except where incurred in respect of an employee;
(c) any penalty or fine imposed under any law for the time being in force.

(3) Where expenditure is incurred partly for the purposes of an assessable business and partly for another purpose, only so much of the expenditure as is attributable to the business shall be allowed.
Section 18. Capital allowances.

(1) Where a person carrying on an assessable business incurs capital expenditure on plant and machinery, an allowance shall be made at the rate of fifteen per cent per annum on the written down value.
(2) An allowance under sub-section (1) shall not be made in respect of any asset in the year in which it is disposed of.
(3) Where an asset is used partly for the purposes of an assessable business, the allowance shall be reduced in the proportion that the non-business use bears to the total use.
Section 24. Input credit on qualifying supplies.
(1) A registered person shall be entitled to credit for tax borne on a qualifying supply received in the course of an assessable business.
(2) Credit under sub-section (1) shall be claimed in the prescribed period in which the supply is received, or in the immediately following prescribed period, and not thereafter.
(3) No credit shall be allowed where -
(a) the supply is used wholly for a purpose other than an assessable business;
(b) the person does not hold a valid tax invoice in respect of the supply;
(c) the supply consists of motor vehicles, save where the business consists of dealing in or hiring out such vehicles.
(4) Where a qualifying supply is used partly for an assessable business and partly otherwise, credit shall be apportioned on a reasonable and consistent basis.
Section 31. Records and retention.
(1) Every person carrying on an assessable business shall keep sufficient records to enable the profits of that business to be ascertained.
(2) Records kept under sub-section (1) shall be retained for a period of six years from the end of the prescribed period to which they relate.
(3) Records may be retained in electronic form provided they are capable of being reproduced in legible form.
Section 40. Penalties for failure to keep records.
(1) A person who fails to comply with Section 31 shall be liable to a penalty not exceeding one hundred thousand rupees.
(2) No penalty shall be imposed under sub-section (1) where the person satisfies the proper officer that there was a reasonable excuse for the failure.
